record.original_question: Suppose that f (z) = z + ∞ n n=2 an z in S and that P (z) = k=0 bk z k is a polynomial of degree at most n. Is it true that max |P (z) ∗ f (z)| ≤ n max |P (z)|? |z|=1 |z|=1 P Here P ∗ f = nk=0 ak bk z k . The above result would imply Rogosinski’s generalised Bieberbach conjecture but is weaker than Robertson’s conjecture, see Sheil-Small [708]. (T. Sheil-Small)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ denote the class of functions $f$ that are analytic and univalent on the open unit disk $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ and normalized by $f(0)=0$, $f'(0)=1$, so that
$$f(z)=z+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}a_n z^n.$$
For a polynomial $P(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}b_k z^k$ of degree at most $n$, define the Hadamard (coefficient) convolution with $f$ by
$$(P\ast f)(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}a_k b_k z^k,$$
where we set $a_0=0$ and $a_1=1$.

Prove or disprove: for every $f\in S$, every positive integer $n$, and every polynomial $P$ of degree at most $n$,
$$\max_{|z|=1}|(P\ast f)(z)|\le n\max_{|z|=1}|P(z)|.$$
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a definitive resolution of this specific inequality of Sheil-Small. It is known that the inequality would imply Rogosinski's generalized Bieberbach conjecture (a consequence of de Branges's theorem) but is strictly weaker than Robertson's conjecture. No source located confirms a proof or counterexample of the precise statement.

status_evidence.title: Hadamard products of Schlicht functions and the Pólya-Schoenberg conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Ruscheweyh and Sheil-Small's work on Hadamard convolutions of univalent functions; the specific inequality max |P*f| ≤ n max |P| is not addressed in available results.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the specific Sheil-Small polynomial-convolution inequality is reported in standard references on Hadamard products of univalent functions.
